Shri Kamal Nath Nayak - Panel Lawyer for the respondents
/S  ORDER
The present petition has been filed for review of order dated 22.11.2023 passed in WP No. 10144 of 2014.

2. It is argued by learned counsel for the petitioner that though his writ petition has been allowed by this Court by order dated 22.11.2023 and he is not aggrieved by that part of the order whereby he has been held entitled to receive compensation from the State.

However, the petitioner is aggrieved by the finding recorded by this Court that the dispossession of the petitioner has taken place in the year 1975-76 to the extent of 1.04 acres of land and therefore, the compensation has been ordered to be paid to the petitioner as per market value on the date of possession being taken over in the year 1975-76 and held entitled to interest as per Section 34 of the Act of 1984 till the date of actual payment from the date of taking possession.

3. It is further argued by learned counsel for the petitioner that initially the land which has been taken possession without acquisition was only 3 meter wide strip in the year 1975 but later on some more portion was occupied by the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-JBP:55572 2 RP-121-2024 State authorities and this resulted in 7.5 meter wide strip in the year 2011.

Thus, it is contended that this Court should order compensation to be paid at rate prevailing in the year 1975-76 for 3 meter wide strip and at the rate prevailing in the year 2011 for the remaining 4 meter wide strip which was occupied by way of road widening in the year 2011.

4. Upon perusal of the documents placed on record in this review petition as well as in the writ petition it is seen that in the writ petition no specific pleading was made by the petitioner that in which year how much wide strip of land was occupied by the State for construction of road.

sentences.text: Court has arrived at the conclusion in the writ petition that private land of the petitioner has been utilized for road construction in the year 1975 based on the documents (Annexure P-6) dated 05.04.2013 and (Annexure P-9) dated 13.02.2014 issued by the State authorities and held that 1.04 acre private land of the petitioner has been utilized for construction of road sometime in the year 1975-76.

Now in the present review petition the petitioner has brought on record document (Annexure R-2) wherein under the Right to Information Act an information has been given by the Public Works Department that earlier the road was 3 meter wide and now its width has been increased after widening.
5.

However, looking even to the document (Annexure R-2) dated 16.12.2015 it is seen that it certifies that earlier also the road was 7.50 meter wide but it was having metalled portion only 3.00 meter wide.

It appears that the remaining portion was metalled by M.P. Road Development Corporation somewhere in the year 2011-12 but the letter dated 16.12.2015 certifies that even prior to widening the road was 7.5 meter wide but having lesser metalled portion.

The petitioner raises a purely disputed question of fact which cannot not be adjudicated on the basis of rival affidavits that what was the width of road up to NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-JBP:55572 3 RP-121-2024 the year 2011 and after the year 2011.

Finding no cause for review or modification of the order dated 22.11.2023, the present review petition is dismissed leaving it open for the petitioner to avail alternative remedies for adjudication of such disputed facts, subject to the law of limitation.
6. With the aforesaid observations, the review petition is dismissed.
